steps.say: Shoulder pain above the elbow is the rotator cuff until proven otherwise. The supraspinatus tendon is involved first in most cases at its critical hypovascular zone. The Neer and Hawkins-Kennedy tests are performed to elicit impingement pain. A painful arc between 60 and 120 degrees is produced by cuff disease.
steps.tx: Painful arc from **60 to 120 degrees** with night pain on lying on the shoulder defines **rotator cuff** tendinopathy, usually the **supraspinatus** tendon wearing out in its watershed segment about **1 cm** above the greater tuberosity footprint. The **Neer** impingement test forces forward flexion against a stabilized scapula, while the **Hawkins-Kennedy** test cranks internal rotation with the shoulder flexed 90 degrees. Both reproduce subacromial pain. A drop arm indicates a large tear, and ultrasound separates partial from full thickness lesions.

steps.say: Elbow pain on gripping is epicondylitis until proven otherwise. The lateral side is affected in tennis elbow at the ECRB origin. The medial side is affected in golfer elbow at the common flexor origin. The Maudsley test is performed by resisted third-digit extension.
steps.tx: Tennis elbow is **lateral epicondylitis**, microtrauma with angiofibroblastic tendinosis at the **extensor carpi radialis brevis** (ECRB) origin, aching with resisted wrist extension and with resisted middle-finger extension called the **Maudsley** test. Golfer elbow is **medial epicondylitis** of the **common flexor** and pronator teres origin, aching with resisted wrist flexion and pronation with the elbow straight. Both are degenerative tendinopathies, so **NSAIDs** only blunt pain briefly while eccentric loading with activity change heals, and stubborn cases receive glucocorticoid injection.

steps.say: Thumb-side wrist pain after lifting a baby is De Quervain tenosynovitis until proven otherwise. The first dorsal compartment is narrowed around the APL and EPB tendons. The Eichhoff test is performed by ulnar deviation with the thumb clasped. A thumb spica with one sheath injection is required for most cases.
steps.tx: Texting-thumb pain over the radial styloid is **De Quervain tenosynovitis**, stenosing inflammation of the **first dorsal** compartment that traps abductor pollicis longus (APL) tendons with extensor pollicis brevis (EPB) beside them. The **Eichhoff** test, thumb clasped inside the fist with the wrist bent toward the ulna, reproduces sharp radial pain, separating it from thumb-base arthritis and intersection syndrome. A thumb spica splint with a single **triamcinolone** sheath injection settles most cases, while repeat failures undergo surgical release of the compartment.

steps.say: Lateral hip pain on lying on that side is trochanteric pain syndrome until proven otherwise. The gluteus medius and minimus tendons are affected rather than the bursa. The single-leg stance test is performed for at least 30 seconds. Load management with gluteal strengthening is required for recovery.
steps.tx: Night pain over the bony outer hip is **greater trochanteric pain syndrome** (GTPS), usually **gluteus medius** and minimus tendinopathy or tearing with secondary bursal irritation, not primary bursitis. Tenderness sits over the greater trochanter, and a **single-leg** stance held **30 seconds** that brings pain confirms it at the bedside. MRI shows tendon splits with peritrochanteric edema when the diagnosis is uncertain. Gluteal loading programs beat repeated steroid shots, which weaken tendons further.

steps.say: Shoulder stiffness without weakness is adhesive capsulitis until proven otherwise. The capsule is thickened and contracted through freezing, frozen, and thawing stages. Both active and passive external rotation are lost by above 50 percent. Diabetes with thyroid disease is found in many cases.
steps.tx: A shoulder that will not rotate outward, actively or passively, is **adhesive capsulitis** (frozen shoulder), dense capsular contracture running from the painful **freezing** phase through the stiff **frozen** phase into the **thawing** recovery phase across 9 to 24 months. External rotation loss above **50 percent** versus the other side is the hallmark, with a scarred rotator interval and obliterated axillary recess on arthrography. Diabetes and thyroid disease predispose. This figure is the display of the thickened capsule. Early intra-articular steroid with hydrodilatation and graded physiotherapy restores motion.

vis.alt: Anatomical cutaway of a glenohumeral joint showing a fibrotic, thickened joint capsule with contracture of the coracohumeral ligament, scarred rotator interval, and obliterated axillary recess.
vis.caption: Frozen shoulder: thickened capsule with scarred rotator interval and obliterated axillary recess. Contracture removes passive external rotation. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Inner knee pain a handbreadth below the joint line is pes anserine pain until proven otherwise. The sartorius, gracilis, and semitendinosus tendons are joined at the tender spot. Elderly obese females with knee osteoarthritis are affected most often. Weight reduction with quadriceps work is required for lasting relief.
steps.tx: **Pes anserine** bursitis with tendinopathy gives focal tenderness about **5 cm** below the inner knee joint line, where **sartorius**, gracilis, and semitendinosus (SGS) join in one conjoined tendon. The classic sufferer is the elderly obese female with knee osteoarthritis and valgus knees, aching on stairs and rising from chairs. Septic bursitis, stress fracture, and referred hip disease are excluded first. A short **NSAID** course with weight reduction and quadriceps strengthening settles most cases without injection.

nodes.label: Inner knee pain 5 cm below line

steps.say: Heel pain with the first morning steps is plantar fasciitis until proven otherwise. The medial calcaneal insertion is tender after rest and eases with walking. The windlass test is performed by passive big-toe dorsiflexion. Calf stretching with heel cups is required before any injection.
steps.tx: Stabbing heel pain on the **first morning** steps is **plantar fasciitis**, overload of the fascia at the **medial calcaneal tuberosity** insertion, easing as the foot warms then aching by evening. The **windlass** test, dorsiflexion of the big toe with the ankle neutral, reproduces the pain and separates it from fat-pad atrophy, calcaneal stress fracture, and tarsal tunnel syndrome. This figure is the display of the fascia with the test. Calf stretching with heel cups, night splints, and weight control forms the base, with one ultrasound-guided steroid shot for resistant heels.

vis.alt: Anatomy of foot's sole showing plantar fascia. Inset illustrates Windlass test: passive first MTP dorsiflexion reproduces medial heel pain.
vis.caption: Plantar fascia with the Windlass test: passive big-toe dorsiflexion reproduces medial heel pain. First-morning steps are the hallmark. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Most soft-tissue pain is managed with load change, physiotherapy, and short NSAID courses. Injections are kept for stubborn cases after the diagnosis is confirmed. Hot joints with fever are tapped urgently and never injected. Trauma with deformity is imaged before any injection.
steps.tx: **Load management** with relative rest, physiotherapy, eccentric programs, and short **NSAID** courses settles most tendinopathies, with image-guided glucocorticoid injection rescuing the stubborn few. **Red flags** change the track: a hot swollen joint with fever indicates urgent aspiration for sepsis, trauma with deformity indicates fracture imaging, and progressive numbness indicates nerve entrapment needing release. Morning stiffness above one hour with swollen small joints indicates inflammatory arthritis, not soft-tissue disease.

points: Short NSAID course, inject if stubborn
